title: Markets closed for Thanksgiving, early close Friday
summary: U.S. stock exchanges are closed on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving. They reopen Friday and close early, at 1 p.m. Eastern time. The bond market is also set to close early on Friday.
why: Fewer people trade on short holiday days. With fewer buyers and sellers, prices can move more than usual, even without big news.

title: Nasdaq erases most of a 4.6% drop
summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell as much as 4.6% during Wednesday's session but closed down just 0.62%. The S&P 500 ended at 7,182.78, down 0.25%, and the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Worries about AI stock prices and inflation drove the early selling.
why: A big drop that mostly goes away shows investors are nervous but still buying on dips. It is a good reminder that the closing number does not tell the whole story of a day.

title: NVIDIA slides again as AI stocks stay under pressure
summary: NVIDIA kept falling on Wednesday as investors stayed worried about how much companies are spending on AI. Other chip makers like AMD and TSMC also lost ground.
why: These companies sell the chips that power AI. If investors think AI spending might slow down, they often sell these stocks first.

title: Inflation rose to 3.8% in October
summary: The government's PCE report showed prices were 3.8% higher in October than a year earlier, up from 3.6% in September. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 3.3%.
why: PCE is the inflation number the Federal Reserve watches most. Rising inflation makes it more likely the Fed raises interest rates, which can weigh on stocks.

title: Jobless claims rise slightly to 203,000
summary: The number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time rose by 1,000 to 203,000 in the week ended November 14. Economists had expected about 197,000. People still getting benefits rose to about 1.76 million.
why: Unemployment claims show how many people are losing jobs. The number is still low, which means most people are keeping their jobs, but a slow rise is worth watching.

title: Fed minutes show most officials expect more rate hikes
summary: Notes from the Fed's October meeting showed nearly all officials expect to raise interest rates again. Two officials voted to raise rates at that meeting instead of waiting. Inflation and heavy AI spending were named as risks.
why: When the Fed raises rates, borrowing costs more for people and companies. That can slow the economy and make stocks less attractive than safer savings.
